title: Artinian deformation criterion for smoothness of an algebraic stack
statement: Schemes and algebraic spaces are as in [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids on schemes, with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and which has a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. An open substack is a full substack whose pullback by every scheme-valued object is an open subscheme. Smoothness, flatness and local finite presentation of morphisms to schemes are tested after smooth scheme atlases of the source, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring with specified residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field], and let $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an algebraic stack locally of finite type. Here local means there is a unique maximal ideal, and locally of finite type means that a smooth scheme atlas has locally finite type composite to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fix $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ over the residue map. For an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$ and local structure map inducing the fixed identification, let $\mathcal F_x(A)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(\xi,\alpha)$ with $\xi\in\mathcal X(A)$ and $\alpha:\xi|_k\xrightarrow{\sim}x$; arrows are isomorphisms respecting $\alpha$. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize. The point $x$ factors through the largest open substack smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ if and only if, for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of these local $R$-algebras inducing the identity on $k$ and every $(\xi,\alpha)\in\mathcal F_x(A)$, there exists $(\xi',\alpha')\in\mathcal F_x(A')$ with an isomorphism $(\xi',\alpha')|_A\cong(\xi,\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 0DZS, lemma-characterize-smoothness, equivalence (1) and (3), with existence of a versal ring from Tag 0DQX, lemma-versal-ring. Situation situation-versal holds over Spec R; Spec k -> Spec R is a finite type closed immersion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-versal-ring-existence] to choose a versal ring $C$ at $x$. Its hypotheses hold because $R$ is Noetherian local, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $\mathcal X$ is algebraic and locally of finite type. By [lem-sfb-stack-maximal-smooth-open] the largest smooth open $\mathcal U_f$ in the conclusion exists.

The right-hand condition is precisely unobstructedness of $\mathcal F_x$: both require essential surjectivity on objects for every indicated surjection, including the marking. The groupoid $\mathcal F_x(k)$ is nonempty and has a unique arrow between two marked objects, namely $\beta^{-1}\alpha$ for markings $\alpha,\beta$. Thus [lem-sfb-versal-unobstructed-adic-criterion] identifies the right-hand condition with adic formal smoothness of $R\to C$.

Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-atlas-versal-completion] to obtain an affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, a point $u$ with finite residue field $k_1$ over $k$, a field $l$ finite over both $k$ and $k_1$, and an isomorphism $p(u)|_l\cong x|_l$. Put $D=\widehat{\mathcal O_{U,u}}$, a versal ring at $p(u)$. The same node identifies $x\in\mathcal U_f$ with smoothness of $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $u$.

Apply [lem-sfb-stack-versal-ring-smooth-span] to $C,D$ and the specified isomorphism over $l$. It gives a complete Noetherian local ring $H$ with adically formally smooth local $R$-maps $C\to H$ and $D\to H$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-formal-smoothness-descent] separately to $R\to C\to H$ and $R\to D\to H$. Consequently $R\to C$ is adically formally smooth if and only if $R\to D$ is. All rings required complete in that node are complete; completeness of $R$ is unnecessary.

The chart algebra $B$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $R$ and $u$ lies over its closed point. Hence [lem-sfb-finite-type-completed-local-smoothness] says that $R\to D$ is adically formally smooth if and only if $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth at $u$. Combine this with steps 2--4 to obtain exactly the claimed equivalence.
